steps.label: Arc-enabled data services
steps.sub: SQL Managed Instance / SQL Server with Azure-style monitoring

steps.label: Nothing physically moves
steps.sub: it's a software layer giving Azure visibility and governance

code:
# On the on-prem or multi-cloud server:
azcmagent connect \
  --resource-group rg-arc-hybrid \
  --tenant-id <tenant-id> \
  --subscription-id <subscription-id> \
  --location eastus

# From Azure CLI, once connected:
az connectedmachine show \
  --resource-group rg-arc-hybrid \
  --name onprem-sql-01
caption: The server never leaves the building — it just becomes visible to Azure Policy and Monitor.

steps.label: Real AWS hardware
steps.sub: an Outposts rack or compact 1U/2U server, installed on-prem

steps.label: Same APIs, CLI, console
steps.sub: provision EC2, EBS, and (rack) even RDS/EKS as if in a Region

steps.label: Built for latency & residency
steps.sub: AWS-native compute physically next to the data that needs it

steps.label: Managed by AWS
steps.sub: operated as an extension of your home Region, not a separate stack

code:
aws ec2 run-instances \
  --image-id ami-0abcd1234efgh5678 \
  --instance-type m5.large \
  --subnet-id subnet-0a1b2c3d \
  --placement AvailabilityZone=us-east-1a \
  --block-device-mappings file://ebs-on-outpost.json

# The outpost-arn on the targeted subnet is what
# routes this to the physical hardware in your building.
caption: Identical EC2 syntax — the only difference is which subnet (and outpost) you target.
